newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: SQUASH-NICOL BEATS ROWLAND TO REACH LAST FOUR.
newsitem.headline: SQUASH-NICOL BEATS ROWLAND TO REACH LAST FOUR.

text.p: Scotland's world number three Peter Nicol reached the semifinals of the World Open on Wednesday with a straightforward 53-minute 15-13 15-6 15-9 win over young Australian Craig Rowland.
Rowland, who put out England's sixth-seeded Del Harris in the second round , could not find the same touch under the severity of the Scot's attack.
Also into the semifinals is England's highest ranked player, fifth-seeded Chris Walker, who put out lacklustre third seed Brett Martin of Australia 15-10 12-15 15-9 15-13 in 55 minutes.
It was Walker's third victory over the 33-year-old Australian in recent months and partly explains why he has overtaken Martin on the latest world ranking list to become world number four.

In later quarter-finals, defending champion Jansher Khan of Pakistan was meeting English seventh seed Simon Parke while the second seed, Rodney Eyles of Australia, played Zubair Jahan, the young Pakistani who survived a fractious match and a fearsome ball strike to the chest on Tuesday against Anthony Hill, another Australian.
Hill may now face disciplinary action for his behaviour on and off court.
